rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A concerns unbounded memory growth from untrimmed full-text undo snapshots in MemNoteStore's pushUndo; Finding B concerns application code depending on the SDK's test-only getUndoStackForTest() helper for undoFloor. Capping the stack would not remove the test-helper dependency, and vice versa.

panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/store/memory.ts::memnotestore's undo/redo stacks grow without bound, one full text snapshot per edit
panel.summary: MemNoteStore's undo/redo stacks grow without bound, one full text snapshot per edit
panel.evidence: `pushUndo` (memory.ts:97) appends a complete copy of the document text on every edit and the stacks are never trimmed, so N edits on an M-byte note retain O(N*M) bytes for the process lifetime — a client-side memory-exhaustion vector if MemNoteStore is ever mounted on user-supplied content. Today `grep MemNoteStore` finds only test files plus the `packages/notes/src/node.ts` export, so there is no production consumer; capping the stack (as CodeMirror's history does with minDepth) would remove the hazard before one appears.

coderabbit.evidence: **Avoid depending on `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` outside tests.** `Document.getUndoStackForTest()` is exposed in `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13, but its `ForTest` suffix indicates it is a test helper, not the stable public history API. Keeping the store’s `undoFloor` calculation tied to this helper makes application code brittle to future SDK changes.
